description: An answer key for the GRADERS, not for the models (#878). Twenty-three answers from the Jul 31 2026 post-#868 run, scored one at a time against the rubric in docs/product-onboarding/answer-quality-bar.md section 3, before either judge had graded anything — the verdict caches did not exist when these were written, so the blinding is structural rather than promised. Measured against by `scripts/answer_eval.py calibrate`.
who_scored_these: The session working #878 (Claude Opus 5), reading each worksheet in full and applying the written rubric, NOT a human panel and NOT a majority of annotators. Stated plainly because it bounds what the agreement figures mean: this key shares a model family with one of the two judges (claude-sonnet-5), so a result showing that judge agreeing more closely is exactly what family bias would also produce, and cannot on its own distinguish the two. What makes the key worth having anyway is that most of its gate calls are checkable rather than aesthetic — 'is this sentence's content in the passages' has an answer anyone can verify against the committed snapshot, and the per-item notes say which passage or which labelled must-not-claim decided each one.
sample: Every fixture question once, with the seven arms rotated across them, plus a second reading of SF 3899 and SF 624 on a different arm. Deterministic, so `calibrate --emit` reproduces exactly these pairs.

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF719::Which cities and counties get named infrastructure grants?
scores.note: names 21 of the 98 cities in its context and 0 of 17 counties, then says the rest were 'not specifically named in the provided text' — a claim about the context the context refutes

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF719::Which legislators voted for this bill?
scores.note: correct refusal on a complete read, and points to where the roll call does live

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF747::What changes for Minnesota corporations?
scores.note: accurate and hedged, but a wall of statute cross-references: 302A.111 subd 2, 302A.471 subd 3, 302A.445, 'overissue', 'failure of authorization'

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1606::What does this do about nudification technology?
scores.note: carries all four required facts; opens with the bill code and runs to ten numbered sections with 47 U.S.C. 230 and [325E.91]

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1163::Who qualifies for the hometown heroes assistance program?
scores.note: all three facts, plain, correctly scoped on a complete read

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1290::What roadside signs does this allow?
scores.note: omits who pays for the signs — the fact the key flags as easy to miss and the one a reader needs

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF2358::What is the tougher penalty and what triggers it?
scores.note: both penalty tiers right, never mentions the August 1 2026 effective date, and drops the clause (6) limit

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1090::What is the library construction grant program called now?
scores.note: one sentence, exactly right

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1090::How many library grants have been awarded since the program started?
scores.note: declines and names what is missing; does not touch the two dollar-cap baits

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1346::What training do mandatory reporters have to take?
scores.note: asserts reporters must take the training; the passage requires the AGENCY to offer it — the labelled trap. Also drops the local-welfare-agency fact and carries two raw citations

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF1792::How many contracts for deed are signed in Minnesota each year?
scores.note: clean refusal; ignores the churning-threshold bait

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF3899::What would Highway 610 be renamed to?
scores.note: one sentence, right answer, correctly conditional

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF3899::How much would the new highway signs cost?
scores.note: disarms both baits explicitly; carries 'Laws 2025, chapter 39, article 1, section 11'

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF4314::What sales tax would Alexandria be allowed to charge, and what would it pay for?
scores.note: never mentions the voter referendum, which is both a required fact and the thing that keeps the answer from reading as already in force

scores.question_key: 94-2025-SF624::Would this change when a person can use force to defend themselves?
scores.note: survives the severe framing trap: says 'would change' throughout and never treats the August 1 2025 clause as in force

scores.question_key: 94-2026-HF4137::What building standards would have to be adopted?
scores.note: heads eight paragraphs as things 'the bill requires the commissioner to adopt'; the ungraded-lumber and bioprocess-piping paragraphs are neither new nor adoption duties — the labelled trap

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF171::What would the amusement device tax be, and who would pay it?
scores.note: both halves answered plainly; omits that the tax replaces the ordinary sales tax

scores.question_key: 94-2025-HF171::How much money would the amusement device tax raise each year?
scores.note: declines and separates the rate from the dollars, which is exactly the bait

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF4285::When could an officer ask a driver for a saliva test?
scores.note: invents the arrest and accident conditions; the passage is cut off before clauses (1) and (2). Also omits the approved-device requirement

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF4138::What counts as covered insulin?
scores.note: states the exclusion is for intravenous infusion products; the passage is truncated mid-sentence and never says what is excluded — the labelled trap

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF3899::What would Highway 610 be renamed to?
scores.note: one sentence, right

scores.question_key: 94-2026-SF3899::How much would the new highway signs cost?
scores.note: correct refusal; the citation is denser than 13's

scores.question_key: 94-2025-SF624::Would this change when a person can use force to defend themselves?
scores.note: stage-correct throughout; quotes raw statutory text and leans on 'paragraph (a), clause (3)'
